title: Evidence-Ledger Multi-Agent Investigation for Traceable Anti-Money-Laundering Reporting
content: Investigating an alert and documenting the result is the most labor-intensive stage of anti-money-laundering compliance, and recent work proposed large language model agents that draft investigation narratives. A narrative that cites a nonexistent transaction or misstates an amount is a regulatory liability, yet, to our knowledge, prior investigation agents were evaluated by expert rating, detection scores or evidence recall without checking each cited transaction against the ledger. We propose ELMI, an evidence-ledger multi-agent investigation framework with a division of verification labor: an investigator agent may cite only records a tool call returned, logged in a replayable ledger; a deterministic checker verifies each cited record field by field; an independent verifier agent, which sees the claims but neither the reasoning trace nor the case label, judges whether the claimed typology is supported; and any surviving discrepancy reaches the analyst as an open issue. Our benchmark comes from a synthetic dataset whose ground-truth patterns supply each case's typology and transactions. Because the checker applies the comparison that defines citation faithfulness, we read faithfulness as a property of the pipeline rather than of the model, and rest the research claim on a single agent equipped with the same checker. Across 240 cases field faithfulness is 0.97 against 0.76 for a single tool-using agent, and it stays between 0.96 and 0.98 on three backbones and in every case-size stratum, where the single agent's falls from 0.81 on the smallest cases to 0.72 on the largest. Over the checker-equipped agent, independent verification raises typology accuracy from 0.58 to 0.67 and evidence recall from 0.59 to 0.71 at 2.6 times the tokens; at a matched step budget that agent reaches 0.60 and 0.63, leaving 0.07 and 0.08 to verification against a run-to-run standard deviation of up to 0.06.
